comparison: Both strongly support the technical advance of 3D light-sheet imaging (C33-C35). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative depth penetration and resolution data, while peer reviewers highlight the novelty and practical utility of the method. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support the finding that high-degree hub cells are centrally located (C3, C36-C38, C82-C83). OpenEval notes the radial pattern as a reasonable interpretation, while Peer Reviewer 3 challenges the 'radial' terminology but accepts the central localization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED despite the minor terminological critique.

Both strongly support findings about wave initiation at periphery (C6, C39) and temporal instability of leader cells (C7, C43-C44, C71, C73). Peer reviewers treat this as a major conceptual advance disproving privileged cells. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address wave instability and stochastic dominance. OpenEval focuses on quantitative movement of wave center and axis rotation (C7, C42-C44, C71, C73), while peer reviewers emphasize the conceptual advance of disproving privileged cells. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support the distinction between regional and cellular stability (C4, C41, C45-C46, C82, C85-C86). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance of retention and KL divergence analyses, while peer reviewers accept the differential regional stability finding. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address KL divergence findings (C47) and mechanistic speculation (C48). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of C48, while peer reviewers accept the findings as SUPPORTED without challenging the interpretation about cellular versus emergent properties.

Both address the speculative claim C48 about cellular versus emergent properties. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN requiring validation, while peer reviewers implicitly support it by affirming stochastic nature without dispute. Divergent evaluation types (UNCERTAIN vs SUPPORTED).

Perfect agreement on methodological superiority of 3D over 2D imaging (C49-C50, C69-C70). Both strongly affirm that 2D planes failed to capture regional versus cellular consistency differences. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with peer reviewers calling it a strong technical demonstration.

Both support GKa effects on temporal dynamics (C8, C52-C53). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation, while peer reviewers affirm GKa influences leader cell phenotype. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, though they address partially overlapping claim sets.

Both support PKa effects on oscillation frequency (C10, C54-C55). OpenEval emphasizes proportional phase reductions and lack of duty cycle effect, while peer reviewers note frequency increase. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support GKa effects on spatial wave properties (C9, C56, C58-C59, C62). OpenEval details multiple spatial analyses showing reinforcement and stabilization, while peer reviewers emphasize metabolic sensitivity of mantle regions. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support lack of PKa effects on wave spatial properties (C11, C57, C60). OpenEval notes no significant changes in retention or stability, while peer reviewers affirm hubs remain stable under PKa. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address network stability under metabolic perturbations. OpenEval focuses on PKa's lack of effect on wave properties (C11, C57, C60), while peer reviewers emphasize hub stability under both treatments (C5, C67-C68, C84). Related but distinct claim sets, both SUPPORTED.

Both support the inference that fuel input patterns waves (C12, C61, C76). OpenEval notes this relies on differential GKa/PKa effects, while peer reviewers affirm metabolic sensitivity of mantle regions can be entrained by fuel input. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on network consistency being unaffected by metabolic perturbations (C5, C67-C68, C84). Both note this contrasts with wave property effects and suggests different control mechanisms. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support differential effects on early versus late phase cells (C63-C64). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance of retention and time lag analyses, while peer reviewers accept the inference about earliest phase cells driving consistency. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address GKa effects on temporal separation (C66). OpenEval provides detailed time lag analysis, while peer reviewers accept this as supporting detail for GKa's role. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address oscillation characteristics (C72, C93). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to discrepancy between observed period and cited in vivo range, while peer reviewers accept the measurements as SUPPORTED without challenging the validation claim. Divergent evaluation types.

Both address speculative mechanisms about α-cell interactions (C78, C87-C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN requiring experimental validation, while peer reviewers treat as plausible SUPPORTED hypothesis. Both acknowledge speculative nature but differ in evaluation type.

Both address relationship between 3D findings and prior 2D work. OpenEval focuses on clarifying central localization in 3D versus 2D descriptions (C80-C81, C83), while peer reviewers emphasize the novel 3D contribution (C3, C36-C38, C82-C83). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address radial pattern terminology (C38). OpenEval treats as reasonable interpretation in SUPPORTED evaluation, while peer reviewers challenge the term but accept central localization in UNCERTAIN evaluation. Minor terminological disagreement.
OpenEval validates lack of photobleaching (C92) as important methodological quality control. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally affirm high data quality.
OpenEval documents GKa-induced Ca2+ plateau in 20% of islets (C51) and notes potential selection bias. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific observation.

OpenEval validates background literature and context claims (C1, C13-C32) as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers do not challenge the contextual framing.

OpenEval validates citations to prior work on glucokinase and alternative hypotheses (C74-C75, C77, C79). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these contextual claims.

OpenEval validates methodological details including ethics approval (C90) and network threshold choice (C94). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific methodological claims.
